findings.description: The script reads a comment-triggered review run's `workflow_run.pull_requests` as "the PRs this review was for". But GitHub fills that array with open PRs whose head branch or head SHA matches the run, and a comment-triggered run's head is `main`. So any open PR with `main` as its head (for example a main→release PR) takes the place of the sweep. The PR that was actually reviewed keeps a stale review label for up to an hour.
findings.body:
**A comment-triggered review run can name the wrong PR.** The script treats `workflow_run.pull_requests` as the PRs the finished review ran for. That only holds when `pull_request` triggered the run.

`Claude Code Review` also runs on `issue_comment` (`.github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml` L18-19), and that run's `head_branch` and `head_sha` are the default branch's. GitHub fills `pull_requests` with the open PRs whose head branch or head SHA matches the run, not with the PR that triggered it. So any open PR whose head is `main` shows up in the array of every `@claude review` run. A `main` → `release` PR is a common setup in adopting repos. The comment at L277-278 ("that run starts from main, so it names no PR") assumes the opposite.

What this causes:
1. **Lost verdict.** L274-275 reconcile only that unrelated PR and skip the sweep. The PR that got the `@claude review` keeps its old label until the hourly sweep or its next event.
2. **Wrong concurrency group.** L69-70 put the run in that other PR's group (`pull_requests[0].number`) with `cancel-in-progress` on, instead of the shared non-cancelling `github.ref` sweep group.
3. **Foreign PRs.** An entry can be a PR in another repository whose head is this repo's `main`. Its `number` then makes `pulls.get` hit an unrelated local PR or return 404, and `reconcileAll` fails the run.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config/blob/1fba3bf44d484aa0f4dbcc3d0d8960aad85b335e/.github/workflows/pr-state-labels.yml#L271-L279
https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config/blob/1fba3bf44d484aa0f4dbcc3d0d8960aad85b335e/.github/workflows/pr-state-labels.yml#L69-L70

**Fix:** trust the array only for `pull_request`-triggered runs (both watched workflows' PR paths are `pull_request`). Apply the same guard in the concurrency expressions, e.g. `github.event.workflow_run.event == 'pull_request' && github.event.workflow_run.pull_requests[0].number || github.ref`, and the same condition in `cancel-in-progress`.

findings.description: `Test adequacy:` No test pins the `claude-review` success description (`N important finding(s)` / `no blocking issues`) that this regex parses. If `post-review.script.ts:236` is reworded, every PR with importants silently gets labelled Approved. A test in `tools/review/test/integration/comment-requested-review.test.ts` that runs the poster and checks the posted description against the workflow's regex would catch it.

Every trigger that names no PR runs a full sweep of about 4-5 GITHUB_TOKEN calls per open PR: each push to main, the hourly schedule, and each comment-triggered review. With a few dozen open PRs this can approach the 1,000 requests/hour GITHUB_TOKEN limit, which the review poster shares.

On per-PR events, any 403 on a label write is taken to mean a read-only fork/Dependabot token. A secondary-rate-limit 403 on a same-repo PR is then logged as a notice and the run goes green with stale labels. Comparing `pull_request.head.repo.full_name` to the repo would narrow it.

The reconcile logic (desired set, null-mergeability carry-over, re-read before writing, 404/403 handling) has no executable check. Moving the script to a `.js`/`.ts` file with an injected `github` stub would let the `tools/review` vitest setup cover it.
Header comment line 5 runs about 140 characters while the rest of the header wraps near 80. Rewrap it to match.
The new labels block splits the review-pipeline list from the paragraph that continues it ("A comment steers a round: `@claude review ...`"). Move it after that paragraph or under its own heading.
`sweep` is a single-caller helper (called only at L279). Inline its body into the final `else` branch (-3 lines), per core.md §Altitude "Inline by default".
`pr.requested_reviewers ?? []` guards a state that can't occur: `pr` always comes from `pulls.get`, which always returns the array. Drop the fallback.
